# Emoji bitmap decoding

Runtime reads the installed system font without copying or distributing the font. CoreText shapes Unicode only; it does not paint color glyphs. The [sbix directory](https://developer.apple.com/fonts/TrueType-Reference-Manual/RM06/Chap6sbix.html) is read from a retained, read-only [CTFontCopyTable](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/coretext/ctfontcopytable(_:_:_:)) reference. Apple documents that table data is not copied. A no-copy Data view keeps the CFData owner alive and never writes to it; no font-file access or TTC face assumption is needed. Only requested glyphs are decoded. PNG/JPEG/TIFF use ImageIO; EMJ1 uses the public Compression framework plus a bounds-checked decoder. No private Apple APIs are called.

EMJ1 prediction, residual and color reconstruction follow [EmojiFonts format documentation](https://github.com/PoomSmart/EmojiFonts/blob/main/EMJC.md) and [decoder](https://github.com/PoomSmart/EmojiFonts/blob/main/emjc.py), which credit [cc4966/emjc-decoder](https://github.com/cc4966/emjc-decoder). The Swift implementation checks dimensions, offsets, stream lengths, versions, and alias cycles. Gender/medical signs without embedded images use vector paths. Unsupported formats fall back to native text so future font updates preserve visible content; current complete-catalog tests require no native text fallback.

The MIT notice is included in Shared/Resources/ThirdPartyNotices.txt and the app license catalog (Vime/Resources/Licenses/emojifonts.txt).

Scrolling uses asynchronous lookahead for the normal path. The compositor produces eager, uncompressed premultiplied BGRA pixels in a CGContext; those pixels do not need an additional UIImage preparation pass. A serial worker publishes ready pixels into a thread-safe cache before scheduling UI callbacks. At `willDisplay`, a cache miss renders only that entering emoji immediately, rather than showing an empty cell or waiting behind speculative jobs. This deliberately trades some foreground work for guaranteed image readiness at the display boundary; frame preparation must be measured alongside missing images. Font references are immutable and each render owns its layout/context, consistent with [CoreText's threading rules](https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/StringsTextFonts/Conceptual/CoreText_Programming/Overview/Overview.html). It never calls native color-glyph drawing. Output pixels are capped at 8 MiB and 240 images, speculative jobs at 96, pending jobs at 192, and main-queue deliveries at 24. Prepared cells retain their images until reuse or panel hiding; closing, appearance changes and memory pressure clear the cache and invalidate in-flight results. These limits exclude images owned by cells, render-server resources and per-render temporaries. See [Emoji rendering](../Architecture/EmojiRendering.md) for lifecycle and verification details.

The EMJC payload format is documented by the community, not a guaranteed Apple API contract. Public CoreText/Compression/UIKit APIs are used, but operating-system font changes can still require decoder updates. Unknown formats fall back to system text rendering; that preserves appearance but does not guarantee the same memory bound. Validate supported operating-system versions and recheck memory after font updates. This implementation does not imply knowledge of WeChat keyboard internals.
